correctness.rationale: Direct elimination of the two equilibrium ODEs at r=Y/X proves X=(ah-cr)/(h+r²), c=b+v(1-hq), u=r(b+v+rX)/h, and u_c=a(b+v)/c. Differentiation yields the published strictly positive lower bound for u'(r); total T-a=r[(ah-c)-(a+c)r]/(h+r²) has derivative numerator h(ah-c)-2h(a+c)r-(ah-c)r² and exactly one positive critical root if ah>c, none otherwise. Perron eigenvalue sign at origin and Dulac divergence -1/Y-1/X-vq/X²-hu/Y² establish extinction/global positive attractor with boundary behavior. Mutant invasion determinant simplifies exactly to (c+Y)(u_hat-u); resident trace is negative. Verified ODE residuals, derivative identities and determinant independently symbolically with SymPy (all zero), after reading actual RESULT.md and 3,664-byte CHECK.py. The finite rational script is supplemental, not proof.

value.rationale: A physically meaningful source/sink biomass-management boundary specifies whether migration loss can be outweighed by net biomass gain and proves uniqueness of optimal export. It distinguishes maximizing total population from the direction of rare-mutant selection with two independent survival losses. Unlike the known qualitative disagreement, its sharp loss-dependent source-sink criterion and quantitative optimum can be directly used in this precise model.

final_claim: For a logistic source with intrinsic a>0 and declining sink -b, bidirectional survival h,q in (0,1), fixed reverse-flow v>0, variable u>=0: total equilibrium biomass has a positive interior optimum iff ah>b+v(1-hq), with unique closed-form r*; all lower-emigration mutants invade a positive-u resident, while u=0 resists higher-emigration mutants.
